gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each single screen under $250 costs per pixel: on 2026-11-21 the Duex Max DS works out at $104.16 per million pixels and the Duex Float 2 Pro at $60.54, so $32.00 more buys 97.5% more pixels.
standout_why: Compared against dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender (pixel totals, PPI, 4.5 W and 7.5 W with the 80% brightness cap), dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender-under-300 (pixel totals, weight comparison), legitproductreviews.com (1.8 lb, 1.3 lb and 2.9 lb weights), deskgearhq.com (no nits, weight, watts or PPI) and itechguides.com's 15-pick page (no PPI, lid weight or watts). Between them they already hold every raw figure; what they lack is the per-dollar arithmetic, the two brightness figures put on the same power condition, and the fact that the 4.5 W figure sits on Mobile Pixels' spec pages for the older non-DS models. deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403, so it was not compared.
decides: It splits the pick by laptop size and does not overturn it. On a 15–16-inch laptop (Mobile Pixels' fit range for the Float 2 Pro) the Float 2 Pro is the better buy per pixel under $250, at $247.99 on a sale price. On smaller laptops, or for a screen beside the lid, the Duex Max DS that ChatGPT picked stays the pick. Both of our linked rows fit the budget only at today's sale prices (list $299.99 and $389.99).

findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender: One, Two or Three Added Screens, and Which Laptops Run Them · Dealectric
findings.note: Diagonal pixels ÷ rated diagonal: 2202.9 ÷ 13.3 = 165.6; 2202.9 ÷ 14.1 = 156.2; 3018.9 ÷ 16 = 188.7. Already on our hub page for the Max DS and Float 2 Pro, and on legitproductreviews.com for all three, so this is not new.

findings.label: Brightness on the same condition as the Max DS (laptop power only)
findings.value: About 280 nits on laptop power (350 nits rated × 80% cap in the 7.5 W Limited Power Mode), against the Max DS's rated 300 nits
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender: One, Two or Three Added Screens, and Which Laptops Run Them · Dealectric
findings.note: The 7.5 W and 80% cap are Macworld's figures as quoted on our hub page; I did not open Macworld. 350 × 0.8 = 280 assumes nits scale linearly with the brightness setting, which is my assumption. legitproductreviews.com (read 2026-11-21) says, citing Macworld, that full brightness needs a 15 W or stronger USB-C charger. The hub states the cap but not the like-for-like nits comparison.

findings.label: Watts per million pixels, each figure with its condition
findings.value: Duex Max 2.17 W per MP (4.5 W maker rating); Duex Float 2 Pro 1.83 W per MP (7.5 W, brightness capped at 80%)
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extender: One, Two or Three Added Screens, and Which Laptops Run Them · Dealectric
findings.note: 4.5 ÷ 2.0736 = 2.17; 7.5 ÷ 4.096 = 1.83. The two watt figures are not the same kind: one is the maker's rated consumption (non-DS spec page), the other is Macworld's limited-power draw as quoted on our hub. The footnote is the finding; the ratio alone would mislead.

findings.label: Weight per added screen, as reported
findings.value: Duex Plus DS 1.3 lb, Duex Max DS 1.8 lb, Duex Float 2 Pro 2.9 lb
findings.source_title: Laptop Screen Extender Review (2026): Is Mobile Pixels' TRIO 3 PRO Worth It? - Legit Product Reviews
findings.note: Per megapixel: 0.63, 0.87 and 0.71 lb. The Float 2 Pro stands on its own kickstand above the laptop, while the Duex models hang beside the lid on magnets, so the weights do not load the hinge the same way (layout from the brief's product records). Mobile Pixels' two spec pages I opened list no weight. A search snippet said the Plus DS manual gives 1.8 lb for the 13.3-inch model, which conflicts with 1.3 lb; I could not read the manual text to settle it.

findings.label: Laptop fit as stated, and by whom
findings.value: "Laptops roughly 14" or larger" is itechguides' wording; Mobile Pixels' product page lists no fit range, per Legit Product Reviews
findings.source_title: 15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026: USB-C, Portable & Triple-Screen Picks
findings.note: The same page gives the Duex Plus DS as for "smaller 13"–14" laptops". The only maker-stated fit among the three is the Float 2 Pro's 15–16-inch range (the brief's record and our under-300 page). The non-DS Duex Max body is 12.6 × 8.9 in on the maker's spec page, which is the nearest maker figure to a fit.
